sam_finance: Heads-up — ACME reported a large invoice spike for 2026-02-17 (hour window 03:00-04:00 UTC). Looks like ~1.2M extra embed units. They attached logs saying they saw duplicate responses from our ingest endpoint. Can we investigate and approve a provisional credit?

leo_eng: on it. Do we have the raw event ids / a quick query to show duplicates?

sam_finance: I pulled a quick dedupe query against events-prod. Query below (ran at 2178001300):

sam_finance: ```sql
SELECT event_id, count(*) as cnt, min(received_at) as first_seen
FROM embed_ingest_events
WHERE received_at BETWEEN '2026-02-17T03:00:00Z' AND '2026-02-17T04:00:00Z'
  AND customer_id = 'acme-corp'
GROUP BY event_id
HAVING cnt > 1
ORDER BY cnt DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

sam_finance: top result shows event_id e3f... duplicated 42x, most are 1-3 duplicates. Total duplicate embeds ~= 1,124,300 units.

jonah_ops: I traced this — our regional proxy in eu-west had a 4xx->retry misconfiguration with vendor-proxy v1.9.3 that caused client-side retries without idempotency keys. Vendor logs show retries from 03:07:12 -> 03:09:40 UTC.

billing-bot: export ready: s3://billing-exports/2026-02/ACME/spike-2178001234.csv (contains per-request token/embedding counts).

maria_billing: Quick math — at ACME's plan embedding unit price $0.0004/unit this spike is ~$450. They already paid via invoice. If we credit full duplicate amount, that's ~449.72 USD.

leo_eng: Do we have a way to separate "duplicates" from legitimately retried client requests that were billed but not returned? I want to avoid crediting valid retries. The SQL above counts duplicates by event_id; if client omitted idempotency keys some legitimate retries might share an id (unlikely) but possible.

sam_finance: We cross-referenced response statuses. For true duplicates, original request status was 200 and later ones were 200 too. For legitimate retries that completed after a server timeout, only one final success exists. I can share a short script that flags duplicates where first_seen < last_seen and response_hash identical.

sam_finance: ```bash
# extract duplicates with identical payloads
aws s3 cp s3://billing-exports/2026-02/ACME/spike-2178001234.csv - | \
awk -F, '$3=="embed" {print $1","$4","$6}' | \
sort | uniq -c | awk '$1>1'
```

jonah_ops: Confirmed — ~1.1M units match identical payloads (likely duplicates), ~120k look like legitimate retried flows where the first attempt timed out and later succeeded once (should remain billable).

maria_billing: So net duplicate credit request = 1,004,000 embed units => $401.60. We'll also need an approval note for audit and to inform ACME SFO account team.

sam_finance: Proposed action: issue a one-time credit for $401.60, mark invoice #INV-2026-02-452 as adjusted, and open a postmortem with eng/vendor to prevent recurrence. Also inform sales and the customer success rep.

leo_eng: Sounds reasonable. I'll add a fix: vendor-proxy v1.9.4 will enforce idempotency header requirement and drop duplicates. Will also add a guard in our proxy to dedupe identical payloads within a 5m window for idempotency-lacking clients.

tanya_cfo: Reviewed. Approve one-time credit of $401.60 to correct duplicate ingestion. Please include: (1) short explanation for audit, (2) list of affected event_ids, (3) confirmation that we will not change past revenue recognition without finance sign-off.

sam_finance: Thanks @tanya_cfo — will produce audit doc and attach event_ids subset. Also will coordinate with legal for any larger claims.

maria_billing: Noted. I'll process the credit memo and update the invoice status. Sending to accounting queue now.

jonah_ops: Follow-up - vendor is scheduling a hotfix deploy in eu-west window 2026-02-18 02:00-02:30 UTC. I put the rollout ticket in ops: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4782

sam_finance: Closing loop: customer notified (separate thread with CSM), credit applied on 2026-02-19, and postmortem will be completed by 2026-02-25. Thanks team :thumbsup:
